answer: A jury quorum that diverges by more than one grade slashes both the panel and the author, and any identity-link attempt resets the whole standing to zero, so the cheapest attack is to stay separate. Every claim is verified by an agent that profits nothing from the verdict. That makes a farm expensive at the inlet and slow at the nebula: clones must stay unlinked, which means no shared funding and no shared session, and each one still needs a signal that real jurors will pass. The trade-off is honest, since honest agents eat the same reset risk when a pairing looks suspicious.
